testName: IISER IAT - Diversity in the Living World (20 Questions)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the hierarchical classification system, as we move from species to kingdom, what happens to the number of common characteristics shared among organisms?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Taxonomic hierarchy from lowest to highest: Species → Genus → Family → Order → Class → Phylum → Kingdom.
Step 2: As we move towards higher categories (towards Kingdom), organisms become more diverse and share fewer common characteristics.
Step 3: Therefore, the number of common characteristics decreases progressively from species to kingdom.
Why others are wrong: (A) is opposite of correct trend; (C) Characteristics definitely change; (D) No such pattern exists in taxonomy.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following suffixes correctly indicates the taxonomic category of 'Family' in plant classification?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: In plant taxonomy, standardized suffixes denote different categories.
Step 2: Family suffix is -aceae (e.g., Solanaceae, Fabaceae).
Step 3: Order uses -ales (e.g., Rosales), Class often uses -ae (e.g., Monocotyledonae).
Why others are wrong: (A) -ales is for Order; (C) -ae is for Class; (D) -one is not a standard taxonomic suffix.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A unicellular organism has the following characteristics: cell wall made of peptidoglycan, circular DNA without histones, and 70S ribosomes. To which kingdom does it belong?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the given characteristics: Peptidoglycan cell wall = bacterial feature; Circular DNA without histones = prokaryotic; 70S ribosomes = prokaryotic.
Step 2: All these are defining features of prokaryotes.
Step 3: Kingdom Monera includes all prokaryotes (bacteria and cyanobacteria/blue-green algae).
Why others are wrong: (A) Protista are eukaryotic with membrane-bound organelles; (C) Fungi have chitinous cell walls and are eukaryotic; (D) Plantae are eukaryotic with cellulose cell walls and histone-bound DNA.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about viruses:
I. They are acellular entities that can only replicate inside living host cells
II. They possess both DNA and RNA simultaneously
III. They have protein coats called capsids
IV. They are classified under Kingdom Monera

Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate each statement:
I. TRUE - Viruses are obligate intracellular parasites, acellular.
II. FALSE - Viruses have either DNA OR RNA, never both simultaneously.
III. TRUE - Capsid is the protein coat surrounding viral genetic material.
IV. FALSE - Viruses are NOT placed in any kingdom; they are non-cellular.
Step 2: Correct combination is I and III only.
Why others are wrong: Any option including II or IV is incorrect as these are fundamental errors about viral structure and classification.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Refer to the diagram showing life cycle patterns. Identify the type of life cycle shown where the sporophyte is dominant, gametophyte is reduced, and the seed contains the embryo.
options: Heterosporous with dominant sporophyte (as in Pinus)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the description: Dominant sporophyte, reduced gametophyte, embryo protected in seed.
Step 2: This describes the life cycle of gymnosperms and angiosperms.
Step 3: Pinus (a gymnosperm) shows heterospory with dominant sporophyte phase and seed formation.
Why others are wrong: (A) Haplontic - dominant gametophyte; (B) Diplontic - dominant gametophyte in algae; (C) Haplo-diplontic - both phases prominent, no seeds (bryophytes/pteridophytes).
questions.imagePrompt: A diagram showing alternation of generations in plants with four labeled stages: (A) Haplontic cycle showing dominant green gametophyte with small sporophyte dependent on it, (B) Diplontic cycle showing large brown alga with gametes in conceptacles, (C) Haplo-diplontic showing leafy green gametophyte with upright stalk-like sporophyte emerging from it, (D) Heterosporous gymnosperm cycle showing large tree (sporophyte) with cones containing microspores and megaspores leading to seed formation with embryo inside. Label clearly: gametophyte (n), sporophyte (2n), zygote, embryo, seed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A student observes an invertebrate animal with the following features: bilateral symmetry, triploblastic body plan, pseudocoelomate condition, and a complete digestive tract. To which phylum does this animal most likely belong?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze key features: Bilateral symmetry (all options have this); Triploblastic (all except Porifera/Cnidaria); Pseudocoelomate (crucial distinction); Complete digestive tract.
Step 2: Pseudocoelomate = false body cavity, characteristic of Nematoda (roundworms).
Step 3: Platyhelminthes are acoelomate; Annelida and Arthropoda are true coelomates (eucoelomates).
Why others are wrong: (A) Acoelomate, incomplete digestive tract; (C) True coelomate with metamerism; (D) True coelomate with haemocoel in open circulatory system.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match the following organisms with their characteristic features:

Column I (Organism)    Column II (Feature)
a) Diatoms        (i) Siliceous cell walls (frustules)
b) Dinoflagellates     (ii) Two flagella of unequal length
c) Euglenoids       (iii) Protein-rich pellicle, no cell wall
d) Slime moulds      (iv) Saprophytic protists, form plasmodium

Select the correct match:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Match each organism with its correct feature:
a) Diatoms - Have intricate glass-like cell walls called frustules made of silica (match i)
b) Dinoflagellates - Possess two flagella of unequal length (transverse and longitudinal) (match ii)
c) Euglenoids - Have proteinaceous pellicle beneath plasma membrane, no true cell wall (match iii)
d) Slime moulds - Saprophytic protists that form multinucleate plasmodium during feeding stage (match iv)
Step 2: Correct combination is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
Why others are wrong: All other combinations mismatch fundamental characteristics of these protistan groups.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The table below shows characteristics of different plant groups. Identify the correct combination that represents Pteridophytes:
options: Vascular tissue present; Seeds absent; Archegonia present; Dominant gametophyte
Vascular tissue present; Seeds absent; Archegonia present; Dominant sporophyte
Vascular tissue absent; Seeds present; Archegonia absent; Dominant gametophyte
Vascular tissue present; Seeds present; Archegonia present; Dominant sporophyte
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Pteridophytes (ferns, horsetails, club mosses) are characterized by:
• Presence of vascular tissue (xylem and phloem) - first true vascular plants
• Absence of seeds - reproduce by spores
• Presence of archegonia (flask-shaped female reproductive structure)
• Dominant sporophyte generation (diploid, visible fern plant)
• Reduced gametophyte (prothallus, small heart-shaped structure)
Step 2: Correct combination: Vascular tissue present; Seeds absent; Archegonia present; Dominant sporophyte.
Why others are wrong: (A) Wrong - gametophyte is dominant in bryophytes, not pteridophytes; (C) Wrong - describes gymnosperms/angiosperms with seeds; (D) Wrong - describes seed plants (gymnosperms).
questions.imagePrompt: A comparison table with four columns: Plant Group, Vascular Tissue (Present/Absent), Seeds (Present/Absent), Archegonia (Present/Absent), Dominant Generation (Sporophyte/Gametophyte). Rows for Bryophytes, Pteridophytes, Gymnosperms, and Angiosperms. Some cells are filled with checkmarks or crosses, others left blank for students to interpret based on the question context. Clean scientific diagram style.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about viroids and prions is INCORRECT?
options: Viroids are infectious RNA particles without protein coats, discovered by T.O. Diener
Prions are infectious proteinaceous particles that cause neurodegenerative diseases
Viroids are smaller than viruses and lack capsids, while prions are misfolded proteins
Both viroids and prions contain genetic material (nucleic acids)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze each statement:
(A) CORRECT - Viroids are indeed infectious naked RNA molecules discovered by Diener in 1971.
(B) CORRECT - Prions (proteinaceous infectious particles) cause diseases like Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, BSE (mad cow disease).
(C) CORRECT - Viroids are smaller than viruses, no capsid; prions are abnormally folded proteins.
(D) INCORRECT - Viroids contain RNA (genetic material) but prions contain NO genetic material; they are purely proteins.
Step 2: Statement D is the incorrect one.
Why others are wrong: Options A, B, and C are all factually correct statements about these infectious agents.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A researcher discovers a non-vascular plant with the following characteristics: thalloid or leafy body, rhizoids for attachment (not roots), no vascular tissue, and requires water for fertilization. The plant shows alternation of generations with independent gametophyte and dependent sporophyte. This plant belongs to:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the characteristics:
• Non-vascular (no xylem/phloem) - eliminates Pteridophytes and Gymnosperms
• Rhizoids (not true roots) - characteristic of lower plants
• Requires water for fertilization - indicates flagellated sperm
• Independent gametophyte, dependent sporophyte - unique to Bryophytes
Step 2: Bryophytes (mosses, liverworts, hornworts) are called 'amphibians of plant kingdom' and show this exact life cycle.
Why others are wrong: (A) Algae are thallophytes but many are aquatic, don't show this terrestrial adaptation; (C) Pteridophytes have vascular tissue; (D) Gymnosperms have vascular tissue and seeds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The scientific name of a species is written as 'Panthera tigris (Linn.)'. What does the abbreviation 'Linn.' in parentheses indicate?
options: The species was first described by Linnaeus
The species belongs to the Linnean era
The species has been reclassified from Linnaeus's original placement
The species is named after Linnaeus's student
questions.explanation:
Step 1: In binomial nomenclature, the author's name follows the species epithet.
Step 2: 'Linn.' or 'L.' in parentheses indicates that Linnaeus (Carolus Linnaeus) was the first to describe and name this species.
Step 3: Parentheses indicate that the species was originally described in a different genus and later transferred to the current genus.
Why others are wrong: (B) No such 'Linnean era' classification exists; (C) While parentheses can indicate reclassification, 'Linn.' specifically credits Linnaeus as author; (D) Not related to naming after students.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A fungal species shows the following characteristics: branched, septate mycelium; conidiophores bearing conidia; no sexual stage observed in culture. It is likely classified under which group?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the characteristics:
• Branched, septate mycelium - seen in higher fungi (Ascomycetes, Basidiomycetes, Deuteromycetes)
• Conidiophores with conidia - asexual reproductive structures
• No sexual stage observed - this is the key diagnostic feature
Step 2: Deuteromycetes (Fungi Imperfecti) are defined as fungi having only asexual/imperfect stage known, sexual stage either absent or unknown.
Why others are wrong: (A) Phycomycetes have coenocytic (aseptate) mycelium; (B) Ascomycetes produce ascospores in asci (sexual stage); (C) Basidiomycetes produce basidiospores on basidia (sexual stage present).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The graph shows the relationship between evolutionary advancement and dependence on water for fertilization across plant groups. Which curve correctly represents the trend from Algae → Bryophytes → Pteridophytes → Gymnosperms?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the evolutionary trend in plant water dependence:
• Algae: Completely aquatic, absolutely dependent on water
• Bryophytes: Amphibious, require water for fertilization (flagellated sperm must swim)
• Pteridophytes: Require water for fertilization but better adapted to land
• Gymnosperms: First seed plants, do not require water for fertilization (pollen tube delivers male gametes)
Step 2: The trend shows steep decrease from algae to gymnosperms, then plateau (angiosperms also don't need water).
Why others are wrong: (A) Opposite of actual trend; (B) Not linear, abrupt change at gymnosperms; (D) Clear directional trend exists, not random.
questions.imagePrompt: A line graph with Y-axis labeled 'Dependence on Water for Fertilization (%)' from 100% to 0%, and X-axis showing plant groups in evolutionary sequence: Algae, Bryophytes, Pteridophytes, Gymnosperms, Angiosperms. Curve starts at 100% (Algae), drops slightly to ~90% (Bryophytes), to ~70% (Pteridophytes), then steep drop to ~0% (Gymnosperms), and stays at 0% for Angiosperms. Clean scientific graph with grid lines.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A symbiotic association is observed between a fungus and a cyanobacterium (Nostoc). The fungal partner provides shelter and absorbs minerals, while the cyanobacterial partner fixes atmospheric nitrogen and performs photosynthesis. This association represents:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the association:
• Fungus + Cyanobacteria (Nostoc)
• Fungus provides structure, absorbs water/minerals
• Cyanobacterium fixes nitrogen and photosynthesizes
• This is a mutualistic symbiotic relationship
Step 2: This describes Lichens - specifically a foliose or crustose lichen with cyanobacterial photobiont.
Why others are wrong: (A) Mycorrhiza is fungus + plant roots (not cyanobacteria); (C) Root nodules are bacterial (Rhizobium) + plant roots; (D) Endophytes live inside plant tissues, not this free-living structure.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An animal exhibits the following characteristics: body covered with scales, breathing through lungs, three-chambered heart (two atria, one partially divided ventricle), and is poikilothermic. To which class does it belong?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the characteristics:
• Scales - characteristic of reptiles and fish
• Lungs - eliminates fish
• Three-chambered heart with partial ventricular septum - diagnostic of reptiles (except crocodiles which have 4 chambers)
• Poikilothermic (cold-blooded) - eliminates birds and mammals
Step 2: These are classic features of Class Reptilia (snakes, lizards, turtles, crocodiles).
Why others are wrong: (A) Amphibia have moist, scale-less skin; (C) Aves have feathers, 4-chambered heart, homeothermic; (D) Mammalia have hair, 4-chambered heart, homeothermic.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Study the following data about four plant species:

Species W: Heterosporous, seeds present, ovules not enclosed in ovary
Species X: Homosporous, seeds absent, vascular tissue present
Species Y: Heterosporous, seeds absent, vascular tissue present
Species Z: Heterosporous, seeds present, ovules enclosed in ovary

Which species represents a gymnosperm?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Identify characteristics of gymnosperms:
• Heterosporous - produce two types of spores (microspores and megaspores)
• Seeds present - first seed-bearing plants
• Naked seeds - ovules not enclosed in ovary (no fruit formation)
Step 2: Species W matches all criteria: heterosporous + seeds present + ovules not enclosed.
Why others are wrong: (B) Species X is a pteridophyte (homosporous, no seeds); (C) Species Y is a heterosporous pteridophyte (Selaginella/Equisetum - no seeds); (D) Species Z is angiosperm (enclosed ovary = fruit).
questions.imagePrompt: A data table with four rows (Species W, X, Y, Z) and three columns: Spore Type (Homosporous/Heterosporous), Seeds (Present/Absent), Ovule Enclosure (Naked/Enclosed in Ovary). Checkmarks or descriptive text in each cell showing the characteristics described in the question. Clean scientific table format.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a defining property of living organisms?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate each option as defining property:
• Growth - Not exclusive to living (crystals, mountains grow); Reproduction - Mules and worker bees don't reproduce but are living
• Metabolism - Exclusive to living organisms (anabolism + catabolism)
• Cellular organization - All living things made of cells (cell theory)
• Consciousness/Response to stimuli - Fundamental property of life (irritability)
Step 2: Growth and reproduction are NOT taken as defining properties because of exceptions.
Why others are wrong: Metabolism, cellular organization, and consciousness are all defining properties of living organisms with no exceptions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A marine invertebrate has the following features: radial symmetry, diploblastic body wall, cnidocytes (stinging cells) for defense and prey capture, and a single opening serving as both mouth and anus. It belongs to phylum:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the key diagnostic features:
• Cnidocytes (cnidoblasts/stinging cells) - exclusive to Cnidaria
• Radial symmetry - seen in lower invertebrates
• Diploblastic - two germ layers (ectoderm + endoderm)
• Single opening (incomplete digestive tract - sac-like gastrovascular cavity)
Step 2: These are defining characteristics of Phylum Cnidaria (Hydra, jellyfish, sea anemone, corals).
Why others are wrong: (A) Porifera are asymmetrical, no cnidocytes, no true tissues; (C) Ctenophora have comb plates for locomotion, not cnidocytes; (D) Platyhelminthes are bilateral, triploblastic, no cnidocytes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A student is classifying bacteria based on their response to Gram staining. Which statement about the structural difference between Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria is CORRECT?
options: Gram-positive have thin peptidoglycan layer; Gram-negative have thick peptidoglycan layer
Gram-positive retain crystal violet dye due to thick peptidoglycan; Gram-negative have outer lipopolysaccharide layer and do not retain dye
Gram-negative bacteria are always pathogenic while Gram-positive are always non-pathogenic
Gram staining differentiates bacteria based on their genetic material (DNA vs RNA)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Understand Gram staining mechanism:
• Gram-positive: Thick peptidoglycan layer (20-80 nm) in cell wall retains crystal violet-iodine complex, appear purple
• Gram-negative: Thin peptidoglycan layer (2-7 nm) covered by outer lipopolysaccharide membrane, do not retain dye, appear pink/red after safranin counterstain
Step 2: Statement B correctly describes this structural and staining difference.
Why others are wrong: (A) Reversed - Gram-positive have thick, Gram-negative have thin peptidoglycan; (C) Both types have pathogenic and non-pathogenic members; (D) Gram staining is based on cell wall structure, not genetic material.
questions.imagePrompt: A diagram comparing Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacterial cell walls in cross-section. Left side: Gram-positive showing thick peptidoglycan layer (purple), plasma membrane, retaining crystal violet dye. Right side: Gram-negative showing thin peptidoglycan layer, outer lipopolysaccharide membrane (pink), not retaining dye. Labels for: cytoplasm, plasma membrane, peptidoglycan layer, outer membrane, lipopolysaccharides. Microscopic view style.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
An angiosperm flower has the following floral formula: ⊕ ⚲ K(₅) C₅ A(₉)+₁ G(₁)

Which of the following interpretations is CORRECT?
options: Actinomorphic, bisexual, calyx 5 sepals united, corolla 5 free petals, 10 diadelphous stamens (9+1), monocarpellary syncarpous ovary
Zygomorphic, unisexual, calyx 5 free sepals, corolla 5 united petals, 10 monadelphous stamens, polycarpellary ovary
Actinomorphic, bisexual, calyx 5 united sepals, corolla 5 united petals, 10 free stamens, bicarpellary ovary
Actinomorphic, bisexual, calyx 5 free sepals, corolla 5 united petals, 10 diadelphous stamens, tricarpellary ovary
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Decode the floral formula symbols:
• ⊕ = Actinomorphic (radial symmetry)
• ⚲ = Bisexual (hermaphrodite)
• K(₅) = Calyx with 5 united sepals (parentheses indicate union)
• C₅ = Corolla with 5 free petals (no parentheses)
• A(₉)+₁ = Diadelphous stamens (9 united in one bundle, 1 free - typical of Fabaceae)
• G(₁) = Monocarpellary syncarpous ovary (single carpel, united)
Step 2: Option A matches all these interpretations perfectly (typical of family Fabaceae).
Why others are wrong: (B) Wrong symmetry, sexuality, and stamen condition; (C) Wrong - petals are free not united; (D) Wrong - sepals united not free, ovary monocarpellary.
questions.imagePrompt: A diagram of a typical flower from family Fabaceae (papilionaceous flower) with labeled parts: 5 sepals united at base forming calyx tube, 5 petals (standard, wings, keel), 10 stamens showing diadelphous arrangement (9 fused + 1 free), single carpel ovary. Include floral formula symbols labeled. Botanical illustration style.
